facts.statement: The genus Scapanorhynchus includes four known species: S. lewisii, S. texanus, S. rapax, and S. raphiodon.
facts.quote: Scapanorhynchus lewisii (Davis, 1887) Scapanorhynchus texanus (Romer, 1849) Scapanorhynchus rapax (Quaas, 1902) Scapanorhynchus raphiodon (Agassiz, 1843)

facts.statement: The genus Scapanorhynchus was first described by Woodward in 1889.
Scapanorhynchus lived during the Cretaceous period, from the Aptian stage to the end of the Maastrichtian stage.
facts.quote: that lived during the Cretaceous period, from the Aptian to the end of the Maastrichtian

facts.statement: While Scapanorhynchus usually did not exceed 4.15 meters in length, the largest teeth found suggest some individuals could reach up to 6.7 meters.
facts.quote: Scapanorhynchus normally did not exceed a total length of 4.15 m, although the largest teeth with height about 6 cm indicate an upper total length of 6.7 m

facts.statement: Scapanorhynchus was likely a pelagic apex predator living in the epipelagic zone or on the continental shelf.
facts.quote: Scapanorhynchus appears to have been a pelagic apex predator that inhabited the epipelagic zone or continental shelf

facts.statement: Isotopic analysis of its teeth indicates that Scapanorhynchus primarily ate fish and occupied a high trophic level.
facts.quote: An isotopic analysis of its teeth suggests that it largely preyed on fish and occupied a high trophic level in its ecosystem

facts.statement: Scapanorhynchus fed on crustaceans, clams, and small fish.
facts.quote: Su alimentación consistía en crustáceos, almejas y peces pequeños

facts.statement: Fossil records place Scapanorhynchus in existence from the Barremian to the Serravallian, between 125.77 and 11.63 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Serravallian (125.77 to 11.63 million years ago)

facts.statement: Some experts suggest reclassifying Scapanorhynchus as Scapanorhynchus owstoni due to its extreme similarity to the living goblin shark, though most specialists disagree.
facts.quote: Their extreme similarities to the living goblin shark, Mitsukurina owstoni, lead some experts to consider reclassifying it as Scapanorhynchus owstoni

facts.statement: Records of Scapanorhynchus from the Miocene, such as S. subulatus, are considered dubious and may actually be misidentified sand sharks.
facts.quote: Later claimed records of Scapanorhynchus, such as those from the Miocene assigned to the species S. subulatus, are highly dubious and may be misidentified sand sharks

facts.statement: A potentially new youngest record of Scapanorhynchus cf. raphiodon was found in Upper Cretaceous (Campanian) strata of the Duwi Formation in Egypt.
facts.quote: A new assemblage of lamniform shark fossils, including possibly the youngest record of Scapanorhynchus cf. raphiodon reported to date, is described from the Upper Cretaceous (Campanian) strata of the Duwi Formation (Egypt)

rejected.statement: Scapanorhynchus possessed an elongated, flattened snout and sharp awl-shaped teeth designed for catching fish or tearing flesh.
rejected.quote: Scapanorhynchus had an elongated, flattened snout and sharp awl-shaped teeth ideal for seizing fish or tearing chunks of flesh from its prey
